summary.headline: Kalyani Forge Q2 FY27 revenue fell about 18% QoQ to Rs 54.4 crore on plant shifts, but EBITDA margin held at 14.2%, a fourth straight quarter above 14%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 54.4 crore, down about 18% QoQ, as a 2,500-ton press was reconditioned and the driveline machining plant was moved from MCD3 to MCD1 over two months. EBITDA margin still held at 14.2% (up 158 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 2.16 crore. H1 EBITDA rose 38.8% to Rs 18.7 crore at a 15.3% margin. Receivables rose to about Rs 141 crore because of a bank changeover that delayed customer remittances and slower lifting by legacy customers. The board approved a Rs 45 crore funding plan (equity about Rs 10 crore, debt Rs 20 crore, asset and inventory monetisation up to Rs 20 crore).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin: management will aim to hold at least 15%, target 18% possibly within FY27 (not guaranteed), and 20% from next year; wants at least six quarters at each level before the next step.
Management described the 14% plus margin as a floor, which is a stated expectation rather than a guarantee.
Revenue: aim to return quarterly revenue to Q1 FY27 levels; expects about 10-20% H2 over H1 growth (per analyst summary of management's answer).

FY28-FY29: tracking revenue growth at customer-account level, targeting 15-20% growth on strategic accounts in FY28; no direct top-line forecast given. Target achieved at about 30% of strategic customers so far.
Working capital: first target 140-150 days cash conversion cycle, next milestone 120 days (quarterly figure, not smooth).

Order book: about Rs 60 crore remaining, down from Rs 90 crore earlier, with Rs 30 crore moved into production over the last three quarters. Existing-product volume ramp-ups of around Rs 20 crore annually are not included.

Rs 45 crore funding: about Rs 20-30 crore for working capital behind planned revenue growth, remainder for capex, admin and contingencies; equity portion mainly from promoters via preferential allotment.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex plan Rs 30 crore: ramp-up programmes about Rs 10 crore, new business Rs 10 crore, future business Rs 5 crore, existing business Rs 5 crore. Rs 8 crore deployed in H1; H2 capex prioritised to machining de-bottlenecking and CV.
Machining utilisation at 85-90%. Condor machining capacity up 10%, with further expansion planned.
Wheel hub line installed up to 30% of planned capacity; sample production started and samples are with customers.
2,500-ton press reconditioned and driveline plant consolidated into MCD1; both lines are back in operation. Activities were fully completed, with some spill-over into November and Q3.
Large engine conrod production started for an OEM serving AI data-centre gensets.
demand_pricing: OEM revenue growth for five consecutive quarters; management chose to protect OEM revenue during the shutdowns.
Steel prices rising; about three price revisions in the last quarter passed on to customers, with pass-through coordinated with suppliers and customers.
Cost levers: Vriddhi Council material-yield projects, power sanction consolidation with utilities, and machine programs and fixtures to cut manual work.
Business development: defence, aerospace and industrial inquiries; a product roadmap is being built on existing capabilities, with no specific programmes disclosed.
EV exposure estimated at 5-10% of revenue; most axle and driveline parts are common to EV and ICE, so growth is tied to passenger vehicle growth rather than EV-specific parts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the H2 operational-efficiency deliverables and the FY28-FY29 road map?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin is the key metric; levers are material cost, power sanction, and manpower productivity. Target at least 15%, with 18% possibly in FY27 and 20% from next year. Revenue growth targeted at 15-20% on strategic accounts in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and how long do programmes run?
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining order book about Rs 60 crore, down from Rs 90 crore, with Rs 30 crore moved into production. Existing-part volume ramp-ups could add about Rs 20 crore annually, not counted in the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 revenue grow over H1 and how will Q3-Q4 run rate look?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact quarterly outlook, but the aim is to return to Q1 levels, with about 10-20% H2 over H1 growth as the endeavour. EV-heavy Q3-Q4 is a focus area.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 45 crore fundraise be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20-30 crore for working capital needed for the planned revenue growth; the rest for capex, admin and contingencies. Debt-to-sales is well below competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why were receivables about Rs 141 crore and what is the DSO target?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank changeover delayed customer remittances as customers updated bank details; collections should normalise in Q3. Legacy customers account for about Rs 10-15 crore. No DSO target given beyond the 140-150 day cash conversion cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Who will invest in the Rs 10 crore equity and how?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly promoters via preferential allotment as a first step, with a larger public equity raise to follow later.

qa_highlights.question: Are defence and aerospace diversification and EV revenue material?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence and aerospace are long-term; products the company supplied in the past, which customers shut down, may be re-entered. More detail is expected next quarter. EV is about 5-10% of revenue.

risks_watch: Receivables of about Rs 141 crore, with cash conversion cycle and debt/EBITDA worsened; the collection normalisation in Q3 needs to be confirmed.
Revenue down about 18% QoQ; the Q3 and Q4 run rate and the 10-20% H2 growth target are not guaranteed.
Remaining order book of about Rs 60 crore is down from Rs 90 crore; new wheel hub and engine orders need to ramp.
Steel price volatility and pass-through lag; power sanction consolidation is still a plan.
Equity component of Rs 45 crore plan is promoter-led; debt and monetisation (up to Rs 20 crore) need to be executed.
Disclosure risk: management is not giving a direct top-line forecast and says it does not want investors to speculate on revenue growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and execution, but cautious and vague on revenue, receivables and quarterly outlook. Management repeatedly said it cannot give exact quarterly guidance and avoided a direct top-line forecast. It attributed the Q2 revenue dip to planned plant and press work and a bank changeover.

growth.why: Management guides H2 revenue 10-20% above H1 and targets 15-20% growth on strategic accounts in FY28, backed by an order book of about Rs 60 crore, a wheel hub line at 30% of planned capacity and Rs 30 crore FY27 capex, though the H2 guide is partly reliant on restoring press and plant output after the Q2 shutdowns.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides a 15% EBITDA margin floor (Q2 at 14.2%, H1 at 15.3%), with 18% possibly within FY27 (not guaranteed) and 20% from next year, backed by material-cost, power-sanction and manpower levers and three steel price pass-throughs in the last quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Wheel hub line at up to 30% of planned capacity with samples out, Condor machining capacity up 10% with more planned, and large engine conrod production for an AI data-centre gensets OEM already started; the 2,500-ton press and driveline plant are back in operation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 revenue 10-20% above H1 and a return to Q1 FY27 quarterly levels (Q1 was about Rs 66 crore vs Q2 Rs 54.4 crore), supported by a Rs 60 crore order book and about Rs 20 crore a year of existing-part ramp-ups not in that book; not guaranteed and management gave no exact quarterly guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Machining utilisation is 85-90%, FY27 capex is Rs 30 crore with only Rs 8 crore deployed in H1, and the Rs 45 crore funding plan includes Rs 20-30 crore for working capital and capex; further machining de-bottlenecking and CV capacity are prioritised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has set an 18% margin target that could come within FY27, but the Q2 revenue drop (down about 18% QoQ) and uncertain H2 growth make an upgrade conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables rose to about Rs 141 crore, cash conversion and debt/EBITDA worsened, the collection normalisation in Q3 is unconfirmed, and the H2 10-20% growth target is not guaranteed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence, aerospace and industrial inquiries are at business-development stage with a product roadmap being built and no specific programmes disclosed; more detail is expected next quarter.

rows.label: Steel price pass-through
rows.why: About three steel price revisions in the last quarter were passed on to customers, and pass-through is coordinated with suppliers and customers, which supports the 14%+ margin floor.

rows.label: Cash conversion cycle to 140-150 then 120 days
rows.why: Receivables are about Rs 141 crore after the bank changeover, with legacy customers at Rs 10-15 crore and collections expected to normalise in Q3; the 140-150 day step is a target, not a guarantee, and the 120-day step is a later milestone.

rows.label: Rs 45 crore funding plan
rows.why: The board approved Rs 45 crore (equity about Rs 10 crore mainly from promoters via preferential allotment, debt Rs 20 crore, monetisation up to Rs 20 crore), with Rs 20-30 crore earmarked for working capital behind the planned revenue growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15% margin floor and on execution of the plant shifts, but cautious and vague on revenue, receivables and quarterly outlook, declining exact quarterly guidance. Analysts pushed on the Q2 revenue dip, the receivables build and the H2 growth target.
